open_points.subject: Repeated import customer identity mapping
open_points.text: A repeated import mints new `customer_ref`s for the Customers it makes; a consumer that kept one the lost import minted relinks it in its own service
open_points.question: What fact maps each `customer_ref` minted by the lost import to the corresponding Customer and newly minted `customer_ref` after the repeated import, so consumers and recorded retention actions can relink it?
options: Keep an old minted `customer_ref` -> v1 `customer_ref` -> new minted `customer_ref` mapping outside Registry until a checked backup holds the import
Make the repeated import reuse the lost import's minted `customer_ref`s
Require the owner and each consumer to identify the corresponding Customer manually from personal values
open_points.default_guess: Keep the old-to-source mapping with the retained import choices, then add the new minted `customer_ref` after reimport.

open_points.subject: Customer restriction and relationship lifecycle after restore
open_points.text: What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures, restrictions, ends of a relationship, the greatest date audit entries were ever erased by — follows the owner's record of the retention review ... naming each action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched
open_points.question: Does the retention record and restore procedure cover the inverse Customer transitions—lifting a restriction and resuming a relationship—or only restriction and relationship-end actions?
options: Record and repeat both directions of each lifecycle transition
Record and repeat only restriction and relationship-end actions
Leave lifts and resumptions for manual correction from the owner's knowledge
open_points.default_guess: Record and repeat both directions, because otherwise a restored backup can preserve a restriction or ended mark that had already been cleared.

open_points.subject: Relationship end date restored after loss
open_points.text: the owner's record of the retention review ... naming each action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched
open_points.question: For an end-of-relationship action, does “its date” mean the action's execution date, the owner-supplied effective relationship-end date required by R0-84, or are both retained so the Customer's ended date can be reconstructed?
options: Retain both the execution date and the effective relationship-end date
Retain only the effective relationship-end date
Retain only the execution date and use it as the end date when repeating the action
open_points.default_guess: Retain both dates and supply the original effective relationship-end date when repeating the action.
